away.headline: Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly suspended for a game for `inappropriate contact' with player
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Fennelly will sit out at Northern Iowa on Wednesday night. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will direct the team that night. AMES, Iowa (AP) — Iowa State suspended women’s basketball coach Bill Fennelly one game Sunday night for “inappropriate contact” with a Cyclones player. Fennelly nudged the player’s head with his hand earlier Sunday in a 69-64 home victory over Illinois Chicago. The 69-year-old Bill Fennelly said last month he plans to retire at the end of the season, his 32nd as head coach at the school. “We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not,” athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. “We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions.” “I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game,” Fennelly said in a statement. “I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward.” The Cyclones are 5-0 this season. Fennelly is 661-335 with 24 NCAA Tournament appearances and 26 postseason appearances at Iowa State. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. By Juan Pablo Aravena in College Football Published: November 17, 2026 at 12:05 pm EST My early Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction looks at whether the Huskers can carry their momentum into a home date with the Buckeyes The early Ohio State vs Nebraska spread leaves little room between the Buckeyes and the home underdog See my Ohio State vs Nebraska spread analysis and Big Ten picks below Ohio State visits Nebraska on Saturday, Nov. 21, with a noon ET kickoff at Memorial Stadium. The Buckeyes are 7-3 overall and 5-2 in Big Ten play after a 28-19 win over Northwestern, which followed a 41-28 loss to Oregon. Nebraska is 6-4 and 3-4 in conference play. The Huskers bounced back from a 24-13 loss to Illinois by blanking Rutgers 31-0. Three points is the key number in Lincoln. Here's my Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction and the price that makes the total my first bet. Ohio State vs Nebraska Prediction Prediction: Ohio State wins a close game; I like the Over more than laying points with the Buckeyes My Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction is that this stays close. The Buckeyes are the likelier winner, but Nebraska has the recent form and the home crowd to keep it within a field goal. Ohio State's offense still runs through Jeremiah Smith. He has 80 catches for 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns. The Buckeyes have been forced to rely on Luke Fahey under center due to the absence of Julian Sayin due to injury. Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards, three touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 28-19 win over Northwestern in Week 11. Bo Jackson gives the Buckeyes balance with 799 rushing yards and seven scores on 159 carries. The question is the defense. Ohio State gave up 41 points to Oregon and 19 to Northwestern in its last two games. Nebraska, meanwhile, just pitched a shutout. Jahsear Whittington leads the Huskers with 5.5 sacks, and pressure on Fahey is Nebraska's best path to keeping this tight. The risk to a close-game prediction is Smith winning outside early. Two chunk completions can put Nebraska two scores behind before its run game gets established. I'd consider the Huskers at more than a field goal; at exactly three, a field-goal loss gets my stake back but doesn't win the bet. Ohio State vs Nebraska Spread Over 41.5 (-108) Under 41.5 (-111) Ohio State vs Nebraska odds via BetMGM as of Tuesday, November 17. Lines can move before Saturday. The Ohio State vs Nebraska spread makes the Buckeyes a field-goal favorite, but the prices aren't symmetrical. Laying three costs -118; taking the three costs -102. If both sides finish the day three points apart in Ohio State's favor, either spread bet pushes. Nebraska's +130 moneyline needs an outright win. That is a different call from my expectation that the Huskers stay in it. I'd rather see whether a +3.5 appears than turn a close-game forecast into an upset bet. The total sits at 41.5. A 24-18 game gets there; 23-17 does not. Shop the number as well as the price across College Football betting apps before Saturday. Ohio State vs Nebraska Big Ten Picks Big Ten pick: Over 41.5 points (-108 at BetMGM ) My second Big Ten pick is the Over. The market expects a low-scoring game, but both offenses have legitimate playmakers. Anthony Colandrea has thrown for 2,297 yards and 18 touchdowns for Nebraska. Kwazi Gilmer has turned 46 catches into 603 yards and seven scores, and Jamal Rule adds 635 rushing yards. Ohio State's last two games produced 47 and 69 total points. Nebraska doesn't have to match the Buckeyes touchdown for touchdown to clear 41.5: two touchdowns and a field goal for the Huskers would leave Ohio State needing 25 points. That fits a competitive game in the fourth quarter. A 24-21 Ohio State win would cash the Over while pushing both sides of the current spread. Chasing a first-half winner would require another forecast entirely; I'm sticking to the full game. The Under wins if Nebraska's defense plays like it did against Rutgers. Colandrea's seven interceptions are the other risk, since empty possessions keep the scoreboard quiet. home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. There's no other way to slice it or dice it, it was disgraceful at best and a 'fire everybody in the whole football department' at worst. Which is what many of the Wisconsin fans are calling for. Maryland had only one Big Ten game all season and had fired their head coach. The Terrapins are a basement-dwelling Big Ten team. So, what does Vegas do for Wisconsin when the Badgers take on another basement-dwelling team, Purdue? Well, they give them barely favorable odds. Can't trust them. The best thing Wisconsin has going for itself in this Purdue game is that it's the Boilermakers that the Terrapins beat a couple of games ago. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. away.blurb: As we do each week, here's how each offensive position group graded out in the loss. Hopkins certainly deserves criticism for his performance, but offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes' questionable play-calling and an inconsistent rushing attack did little to put him in an ideal position to succeed. Darrion Dupree handled the bulk of the workload, rushing 14 times for 57 yards (4.1 YPC) and two scores while adding four receptions for 21 yards. The junior was responsible for both Wisconsin touchdowns, scoring from four yards out in the first quarter and punching in a one-yard run early in the fourth. However, his third-quarter fumble proved devastating, handing Maryland possession deep in Wisconsin territory and setting up a touchdown that gave the Terrapins their first lead. The offensive line's continued inability to establish consistent running lanes complicates the evaluation, and Dupree had his share of positive moments. Nevertheless, his costly turnover and the group's limited overall production prevent a higher grade. Sama's lack of touches was difficult to understand, and his role in the offense moving forward will be worth monitoring. Hilton continues to show flashes of considerable potential, making his limited production particularly frustrating. That general sentiment can be applied to the receiving corps as a whole, which has struggled to establish any consistency amid the offense's recurring dysfunction. Wisconsin's tight ends offered little in the passing game and continued to struggle as blockers, making this one of the offense's most disappointing position groups. Ryan Schwendeman was involved in a botched fourth-and-short exchange in the first quarter that resulted in a lost fumble, although the official scoring charged Hopkins with the turnover. The decision to hand the ball to Schwendeman rather than a running back or attempt a quarterback sneak was another questionable call from Grimes. away.headline: Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense
away.blurb: Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3) suffered a frustrating 24-21 loss Saturday at Maryland (4-6, 2-5), a result that only intensified questions surrounding the program's direction . Having already handed out grades for the offense , Badgers On SI now breaks down the defense and special teams. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. McCoy carried a probable designation earlier this week as Louisville prepared for another road game. On3's Pete Nakos shared an update Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, indicating that McCoy will return against the Tar Heels after nearly a month away, according to his sources. The junior transferred from Florida State after spending two college seasons with the Seminoles. His return gives coach Jeff Brohm another receiving option as the Cardinals continue their conference schedule. Josh Davis, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sat, November 14, 2026 at 5:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Louisville football 's receiving corps has an encouraging injury development ahead of Saturday night's ACC road matchup vs. North Carolina. Wide receiver Lawayne McCoy has been sidelined with a knee injury since the Cardinals' October 17 victory at Syracuse. He missed games against Stanford and Georgia Tech, leaving Louisville without one of their most productive targets. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCoy has recorded 25 receptions for 513 yards and four touchdowns in seven games this season. His 20.5 yards per catch gives quarterback Lincoln Kienholz and Louisville's offense a downfield threat . He ranks second on the team in receiving yards and leads the Cardinals in touchdown catches. McCoy's last appearance produced five receptions for 93 yards against Syracuse before the injury interrupted his season. North Carolina enters at 5-4. Kickoff at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT on ESPN2. Nakos' report did not specify a snap count or any workload restriction. While McCoy is set to rejoin the passing attack, the extent of his involvement remains undetermined before kickoff. The Cardinals head into Saturday's matchup expecting one of the team's leading receivers back following his two-game absence. away.headline: North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury
away.blurb: A potential two-month recovery timeline could put Avdalas in position to return around January, although North Carolina has not announced a specific return date. North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. Virginia Tech Athletics Thomas Hughes · Virginia Tech Hokies On SI Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads BLACKSBURG -After a 23-point loss to SMU in Dallas, Virginia Tech football takes on Stanford in a Saturday night showdown in Lane Stadium. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Wright, Austin, Bright, Terry) Wide Receiver: 2 (Peterkin, Stuewe) Virginia Tech (6-3, 3-3 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) and Boston College (21-14). The Hokies claimed their largest margin of victory since 1922 with their 70-point win over the Keydets Sept. 5, and they avenged their loss from Sept. 13, 2025, against the Monarchs which forced the ouster of then-head coach - and Virginia Tech's current defensive coordinator/linebackers coach - Brent Pry one day later. Against Maryland, the Hokies broke a 15-game Power Four non-conference losing streak dating back to 2017, beating the Terrapins by nine. Sept. 26's victory in Boston College was harder to come by, but amid a nor'easter, sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s career-high 209 rushing yards proved enough for the Hokies to escape with the victory. The Hokies sustained their first loss on Oct. 2, falling to Pitt 35-33 after conceding a 35-10 run over two-plus quarters. Virginia Tech made a nine-point rally to pull within two, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard field goal attempt for the win was ruled no good. The Hokies lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley the following week, ceding the game-winning touchdown to the Golden Bears with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech returned to the win column on Oct. 17, defeating Georgia Tech 34-24 in a contest where it led 24-3 at intermission. The Hokies then became bowl eligible with a 20-16 win over Clemson - their first over the Tigers since 2007 in their trip to Memorial Stadium since 2012. Playing the role of spoiler this week are the Michigan Wolverines (5-5). Michigan has not lived up to expectations in their first year under Kyle Whittingham, as they’re currently scraping by to make a bowl game. With UCLA and Ohio State on the schedule, Michigan needs a massive upset win to reach bowl eligibility. Could it happen here? Not many people believe so, and the market pegs UCLA as a- 3.5-point road favorite with a game total of 37.5 points. In other words, don’t expect many points from either team. Will Michigan start Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood this week? Whittingham said the two will battle it out after Carr replaced Underwood in the 31-7 loss to Oregon. UCLA outlasted Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night, but not without drama. The Bruins Ty Dieffenbach went down with an injury in the second quarter, then returned on the first drive of the fourth quarter following the Illini’s first score of the game (12-7). Like UCLA has done all season, they scored 10 points in the fourth quarter and had explosive plays left and right. UCLA built on their nation-leading 30 takeaways with three interceptions off Illinois and held the Illini to 240 total yards of offense. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. When he returned back to the sideline and re-entered the game in the second half, it gave the Bruins the surge they needed to keep their perfect season alive. Dieffenbach threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns while overcoming his injury, and No. 4 UCLA remained unbeaten with a rain-soaked, 22-14 victory over Illinois on Friday night. “The confidence I think that was gained from that, from him being back, and the confidence he was portraying and showing to them, exuding, that was certainly something that they all felt and understood,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said. Aiden Mizell had six catches for 176 yards and a touchdown, and Semaje Morgan added 56 yards receiving and a score for UCLA (10-0, 7-0 Big Ten, No. 4 CFP). Dieffenbach left with 35 seconds to go in the first half after he fell hard on his left elbow and humerus following a hit by defensive lineman Carter Janki. Third-stringer Madden Iamaleava played the next three series for the Bruins as Dieffenbach remained in the locker room with his arm feeling “nervy”, according to Chesney. Dieffenbach returned with 55 seconds left in the third quarter to a loud ovation from the crowd. He led UCLA on an eight-play, 75-yard scoring drive on his first drive back, capped by a 26-yard touchdown pass to Morgan. “That crowd reaction was unbelievable,” Dieffenbach said. “I mean, that was one of the best moments of my life hearing that crowd. Oddsmakers currently list the Wolverines as 5.5 to 6.5-point underdogs for the team’s final home game of the 2026 season (3:30 p.m., CBS). But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. On Tuesday Night, the first injury report revealed the status of Jordon Davison, Douglas Utu, Jerry Mixon, Bear Alexander, and, surprisingly, Michigan State backup QB Cam Fancher. The best news for the Oregon Ducks was that offensive lineman Douglas Utu did not appear on the first injury report. The veteran guard missed time in the second half with what appeared to be a leg injury, but it appears that he'll return to the lineup this weekend. Defensive Tackle Bear Alexander appeared to have suffered an ankle injury vs. Michigan, but he returned to the game and is probable for Friday Night's matchup. Where the concerns start for Dan Lanning's group is with the status of linebacker Jerry Mixon, who missed the Michigan game. It was stated that Jerry Mixon tweaked something in warmups for the showdown with the Wolverines, but based on the fact that he's doubtful for this weekend's game, it appears to be more serious than a simple tweak. Even more disappointing is the status of Jordon Davison, who's been out since the first half of the Northwestern game. Dan Lanning shared that Davison was out of his walking boot, but he won't return to the field this weekend, putting all eyes on the showdown with the Huskies to end the season. Milivojevic remains out. Making matters more concerning for the Spartans is the fact that backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed as questionable, as they could be forced to turn to their third-string QB against a stout Oregon defense. As the week goes on, the Spartans side of the report is going to be important to follow with 7 players listed as questionable, which can truly go either way. The good news for Oregon is that they're far from the only team dealing with serious injury issues, but it's also disappointing to see how many teams have been knocked down a level with all these injuries. home.headline: Michigan State injury report: QB Milivojevic out; 7 questionable
home.blurb: Starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic is listed as out for Michigan State against No. 14 Oregon on the availability report released by the Big Ten on Nov. 17. Backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed as questionable. Updates to the report are due the next two days before a final report two hours before Friday's 8 p.m. kickoff. In total, 10 Michigan State players are listed out, and seven are listed questionable, which is an improvement from 12 players listed out a week ago. Among those listed out are safety Devin Vaught, linebacker Jordan Hall, tight end Jayden Savoury, and defensive tackle Ben Roberts, the latter who reaggravated a knee injury after two snaps against Washington in a 21-14 loss Nov. 14. For Oregon, outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti is among eight players listed out. Inside linebacker Jerry Mixon is questionable, while defensive lineman Bear Alexander is probable. Also out for the Ducks remains Detroit King alumnus Dante Moore, who has not played since being hit while going down for a slide in a Sept. 26 win over Southern Cal. Milivojevic (left arm) will miss his second game of the season. He was unavailable for an Oct. 24 loss to UCLA at the Rose Bowl, where true freshman Kayd Coffman made his first career start. The East Kentwood product might start again if Fancher (right knee) cannot play. Coffman threw completions on his first four passes including a touchdown, but has since thrown seven incompletions including an interception. Alongside Fancher, wide receiver Rodney Bullard Jr., running back Jaziun Patterson, cornerback Tre Bell, nickelback Michael Richard, left guard Conner Moore and tight end Brennan Parachek are listed as questionable. Bell was a game-time decision against Washington but did not play. Moore injured his right knee one snap before Milivojevic's injury, while Richard went down in the second half and did not return. The story of Michigan State’s football season could be told through its injury report. Its best summary is the data: Out of 42 players to start at least one game, 13 of them are out or questionable accounting for a combined 80 starts out of 220 as a team. On offense, Michigan State is missing 1,559 snaps, 20 percent of its season total. On defense, 2,657 missing snaps account for a loss of 40 percent. away.blurb: Lane Kiffin’s debut season as the LSU Tigers’ head coach is effectively over. The team is 6-4 overall and 3-4 in SEC play heading into the final stretch of the regular season with the College Football Playoff well out of reach. Half a decade later, Kiffin’s Tigers are slumping as the Vols already have their eyes set on the CFP. After Saturday’s game at Neyland Stadium, LSU will close out the regular season at Arkansas, hoping to finish above .500. Tennessee will travel to Vanderbilt, with the aim of clinching a top seed and first-round bye in the playoffs. That’s not what NCAA football fans were expecting when the program hired Kiffin to a seven-year, $91 million contract a year ago. But this Saturday brings a valuable test for Kiffin to give fans some sense of hope for the future, as LSU travels to No. 8 Tennessee. The Volunteers (8-2, 5-2) are already gearing up for the Playoff. Speaking ahead of the massive SEC showdown, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel made it clear what he expects from Vols’ faithful with Kiffin coming to town. “Certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off,” Heupel said. “So, whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they got reinforcements on the golf balls. Hopefully, Knoxville’s ready for his arrival.” More news : Paul Finebaum Fires Back at Curt Cignetti Over Indiana’s Schedule When Kiffin, who formerly coached the Vols in 2009, returned to Neyland Stadium with Ole Miss in October 2021, he received a reception he probably won’t forget. Kiffin had left Tennessee after just one season in 2009 to take the head coaching job at USC, leaving plenty of resentment among the fanbase. Things boiled over late in the fourth quarter of Ole Miss’ 31-26 victory when officials ruled that Tennessee had come up short on a crucial fourth-down play with 54 seconds remaining. Angry fans began throwing everything they could find onto the field, including water bottles, cans, a French’s mustard bottle, and a golf ball that actually struck Kiffin. The chaos resulted in a roughly 20-minute delay, and Tennessee was subsequently hit with a $250,000 fine from the SEC. Kiffin even kept the golf ball as a souvenir. More news : Joel Klatt Names Clear Favorite in College Football as CFP Race Heats Up More news : Philip Rivers Shares Heartfelt Message After Taking Over at NC State While Kiffin might already be mentally on to 2027, Heupel is pushing hard to get this team back in the national championship conversation. Although the exact injury is currently unknown, it does appear his right knee is in a cast in the video shared on X. The injury took place during the second quarter of Tennessee's matchup against Texas A&M. Matthews fell awkwardly to the ground while being tackled by multiple Aggies after making a catch. He left the game with two receptions for 42 yards. Mike Matthews has been one of Tennessee's top options in the passing game throughout the 2026-27 season, appearing in every game so far this year. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. After going a combined 22-6 from 2023 through 2024, they're now 16-7 from the start of 2025 through Week 11 of this year's college football season. Quarterback Kevin Jennings returned for his final year at the helm. In some ways, he's having the season many thought he would, but his abilities as a runner have not been utilized by the offensive coaching staff. To a degree, it's understandable given the talent on the perimeter with players like Yamir Knight , Jalen Cooper , Yannick Smith , Jalen Hale , Theo Melin Ohrstrom and Randy Pittman Jr. requiring a lot of touches. Their defense has been the area of struggle this season, as it was last season. In many areas, Maurice Crum Jr ., a former Notre Dame captain at linebacker, has changed the outlook of the defense for the better. But they're a 'feast or famine' type of unit ranking 13th in the country in tackles for loss and 20th in the country in sacks but also ranking 110th in the country in passing touchdowns allowed and 128th in the country in red zone scoring allowed. This season, when they've faced offenses that can score, they've allowed 41 points to Louisville, 30 points to Syracuse and 49 points to Wake Forest. away.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. home.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
home.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. Full Notre Dame availability report Will Black, offensive lineman — concussion Francis Brewu, defensive lineman — left knee Brauntae Johnson, safety — left foot Jason Onye, defensive lineman — right knee Drayk Bowen, linebacker — right ankle Christopher Burgess Jr., defensive lineman — left tibia Tiki Hola, defensive lineman — right knee DJ McKinney, cornerback — right ankle Stay up to date on local news with WNDU on-air and online. home.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
home.blurb: The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 18, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. home.headline: Major injury update for Georgia Football-Missouri game: Why It Really Matters for the Bulldogs
home.blurb: But the Bulldogs have been struck by injuries at critical positions the last two seasons in the CFP. In 2024, Georgia football starting QB Carson Beck suffered a season-ending injury in the SEC Championship Game - paving the way for Gunner Stockton to make his first career start against Norte Dame in the Sugar Bowl. That injury coupled with turnovers turned out to be too much for the Dawgs to overcome. Only two players are listed on Georgia football's injury report - DL Josh Horton and LB Amaris Williams. Williams was expected to be out, but Horton is a new addition to the injury repot. Horton is listed as questionable for the contest; Williams is listed as out, which means he will not play in the contest. Meanwhile, Missouri has four players listed as out: DL Langden Kitchen, RB Malae Fonoti, OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman. It should be noted that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss is listed as probable for the Rebels' game this weekend at Oklahoma. He joins a a list of 17 other Rebels on the injury report after Georgia's 42-7 beating of Ole Miss in Oxford. The Dawgs, on the whole, continue to be pretty healthy in the grand scheme of things. Should Isiah Canion and Chauncey Bowens return to full health the Bulldogs could become even lethal on the offensive side of the ball. Coach Kirby Smart said earlier this week that Bowens was not 100% healthy. Meanwhile, it will be curious to see if Amaris Williams will return this season. He suffered an ALC injury in the spring, and although the timeline would be tight, it is not out of the question that he could return to play in the playoffs the same way WR George Pickens did at the end of the 2021 season. Pickens also had an ACL injury around the same time that year. home.headline: Missouri football injury updates: Official SEC report Wednesday before Georgia
Georgia football injury report vs. Missouri
All-SEC Georgia star's status in doubt vs. Missouri
home.blurb: However, Georgia has two new players that popped up on the injury report. Georgia starting center Drew Bobo, an All-SEC pick, is doubtful to play. It is unclear what Bobo's injury is, but if he misses the game, then that would be significant for the Georgia offensive line, which is coming off a dominant performance against Ole Miss. Georgia missed Bobo last year in the SEC championship and the postseason. He's a critical part of the Georgia offense. Up front, Georgia's Josh Horton is questionable. Horton is a new player listed on the injury report and has seven tackles and two sacks this season. Pass rusher Amaris Williams remains out for Georgia after tearing his ACL in spring practice. Georgia has some banged up players that aren't on the injury report. Running back Dante Dowdell remains out and running back Chauncey Bowens did not play against Ole Miss despite not having an injury designation. "He's not 100%," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on Bowens. "Just because someone is dressed out and cleared does not mean that they're able to go out there and play and perform. He's working his tail off to get back." away.headline: Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Stanford: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies?
away.source: Virginia Tech Hokies On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/virginiatech as Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Stanford: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? . BLACKSBURG — After a 23-point loss to SMU in Dallas, Virginia Tech football takes on Stanford in a Saturday night showdown in Lane Stadium. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Wright, Austin, Bright, Terry) Wide Receiver: 2 (Peterkin, Stuewe) Virginia Tech (6-3, 3-3 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) and Boston College (21-14). The Hokies claimed their largest margin of victory since 1922 with their 70-point win over the Keydets Sept. 5, and they avenged their loss from Sept. 13, 2025, against the Monarchs which forced the ouster of then-head coach — and Virginia Tech's current defensive coordinator/linebackers coach — Brent Pry one day later. Against Maryland, the Hokies broke a 15-game Power Four non-conference losing streak dating back to 2017, beating the Terrapins by nine. Sept. 26's victory in Boston College was harder to come by, but amid a nor'easter, sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s career-high 209 rushing yards proved enough for the Hokies to escape with the victory. The Hokies sustained their first loss on Oct. 2, falling to Pitt 35-33 after conceding a 35-10 run over two-plus quarters. Virginia Tech made a nine-point rally to pull within two, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard field goal attempt for the win was ruled no good. The Hokies lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley the following week, ceding the game-winning touchdown to the Golden Bears with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech returned to the win column on Oct. 17, defeating Georgia Tech 34-24 in a contest where it led 24-3 at intermission. The Hokies then became bowl eligible with a 20-16 win over Clemson — their first over the Tigers since 2007 in their trip to Memorial Stadium since 2012. Virginia Tech, however, fell in a 51-28 blowout at SMU Nov. 6, allowing season-highs in both points (51) and total yards of offense (569). The 51 points the Mustangs totaled on Virginia Tech were the most allowed by a Hokies team since the 2021 Pinstripe Bowl against Maryland, while the 569 yards Tech allowed were the most since Oct. 10, 2020, against North Carolina. away.headline: Virginia Tech injury report for Stanford paints a promising outlook for Justin Terry
away.blurb: In the Hokies Week 3 35-26 victory over Maryland, Virginia Tech lost offensive lineman Justin Terry in the first half, and he has been out since then. However, there could be some light at the end of the tunnel for Terry in terms of getting back onto the field, and it might come as soon as this upcoming weekend when Stanford visits . That certainly would be a positive, but a return on Saturday night feels a little ahead of schedule. It would be surprising if he were rushed back from an injury to play against the Cardinal. Franklin said that Terry will likely be a game-time decision. "It's not like we're totally through it," Franklin said. "We still got the rest of the week, and probably will come down to either a game-time decision, or it will be he's cleared, but we still don't feel like he's gotten enough reps." Three regular-season games remain in the 2026 campaign, and already at 6-3, the Hokies are guaranteed a bowl game later next month before the attention shifts toward the 2027 season. Getting Terry back would be a big addition, but even if he does return this weekend, his snaps might be limited; just his presence would be big for Grunkemeyer and the rest of the offense. Virginia Tech football comes out of bye week getting healthier in one pivotal area Going all the way back to the summer, injuries along the offensive line have been an issue for first-year Virginia Tech football coach James Franklin. Then, it carried over into the regular season, where it seems that when it rains, it pours. James Franklin gives positive Justin Terry injury update ahead of Stanford game According to Andy Bitter of Tech Sideline , Terry was going through 1-on-1 drills with the D-linemen. After practice, Franklin gave an update on his linemen ahead of Stanford visiting on Saturday night at Lane Stadium. "So today was really the first day that we've been able to have him for everything," Franklin said , per Virginia Tech Athletics ' YouTube . "We've been kind of working him in slowly. Drills, (individuals), one-on-ones. So today was the first day we've kind of had him for everything. So he's getting closer, and it's positive for us.'' Virginia Tech's offensive line can use all the help it can get If and when Terry comes back, it'll be a welcome sight for Hokies fans. To say that the offensive line has struggled this season would be an understatement. Some of that is because of injuries, while some of it is because there have been guys moved around to different positions. Consistency is key and it feels like there hasn't been much of it this season. Virginia Tech has struggled to protect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer at times, despite the Penn State transfer having a good year statistically.
